title: Differentiation of Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells to Brain Microvascular Endothelial Cell-Like Cells with a Mature Immune Phenotype
protocol: Aliquot 2.5 mg of matrix gel into 50 mL centrifuge tubes for storage at -20 °C for up to 6 months.
Add 30 mL of cold Dulbecco's modified Eagle's medium/nutrient mixture F-12 (DMEM/F12) to the tube.
Mix gently by pipetting until the gel has thawed.
Add 500 μL of the solution to each well of a 12-well plate.
Place the plate in an incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2) for at least 1 h.
Dissolve the ROCK inhibitor in sterile water to a concentration of 10 mM.
Aliquot the ROCK inhibitor stock solution into 100-200 µL volumes and store at -20°C.
Make a 100 mg/mL stock solution of L-ascorbic acid by dissolving 5 g of L-ascorbic acid in 50 mL of sterile water.
Store the L-ascorbic acid stock solution at -20°C.
Add 6.25 mL of glutamine to 500 mL of advanced DMEM/F12 medium.
Add 305 μL of L-ascorbic acid stock solution into 500 mL of advanced DMEM/F12 medium to prepare LaSR medium.
Store the LaSR medium at 2-8°C for up to 2 weeks.
Dissolve CHIR99021 in undiluted dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) to a final concentration of 10 mM.
Aliquot the CHIR99021 solution into 100-200 µL volumes and store at -20°C for up to 1 year.
Prepare DMEM/F12-10 medium by adding 50 mL of heat-inactivated fetal bovine serum to 450 mL of DMEM/F12.
Store the medium at 2-8 °C for up to 1 month.
Prepare flow buffer-1 by adding 33.3 mL of 7.5% bovine serum albumin (BSA) to 467 mL of Dulbecco's phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Store at 2-8 °C for up to 6 months.

Begin differentiation when the hiPSC colonies in a 6-well plate show no spontaneous differentiation and have the appropriate density for passaging, typically around 80% confluency (2.5-3.5 x 10^6 cells).
Carefully monitor spontaneously differentiated cells under the microscope to ensure whether multiple passages are required to eliminate non-differentiated cells.
Aspirate the medium from the wells.
Add 1 mL of dissociation reagent to the wells and incubate for 5-7 min at 37 °C.
Dissociate and singularize the cells by pipetting the dissociation reagent solution gently over the surfaces of the wells two or three times.
Transfer the detached cells into a 15 mL tube containing 4 mL of hiPSC maintenance medium.
Resuspend the cells thoroughly in the tube.
Reserve a 10 μL aliquot for cell counting.
Pellet the cells by centrifuging for 5 min at 200 x g at 20-25 °C.
Count the cells and calculate the required volume to achieve a density of hiPSCs (75-400 x 10^3 per well) in a basement membrane matrix-coated 12-well plate.
Aspirate the coating solution from the wells.
Add 1 mL of hiPSC medium containing 10 µM ROCK inhibitor into each well.
Aspirate the supernatant after centrifuging.
Dissociate the pellet in 1 mL of hiPSC medium.
Add the required volume of hiPSC to each well of the 12-well plate.
Place the plate in an incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Evenly distribute the cells by gently sliding the plate back and forth and then side to side.
Exchange the medium with 2 mL of hiPSC maintenance medium lacking ROCK inhibitor on Day -2.
Exchange the medium with 2 mL of fresh hiPSC maintenance medium on Day -1.
Replace the hiPSC maintenance medium in each well with 2 mL of LaSR medium containing 8 µM CHIR99021 on Day 0.
Aspirate the medium and add 2 mL of fresh LaSR medium containing 8 µM CHIR99021 on Day 1.
On Days 2, 3, and 4, replace the medium with 2 mL of fresh LaSR medium lacking CHIR99021.
Aspirate the medium on Day 5.
Add 1 mL of dissociation reagent to each well on Day 5.
Incubate for 6-8 min at 37 °C.
Dissociate and singularize cells with a micropipette on Day 5.
Pass the cell suspension through a 40 µm cell strainer into a 50 mL tube containing 10 mL of DMEM/F12-10 medium.
Stop the digestion reaction by adding DMEM/F12-10 medium (up to 50 mL).
Pipette thoroughly and reserve 10 µL for counting cells.
Pellet the cells by centrifuging for 5 min at 200 x g at 20-25 °C.
Remove the supernatant after centrifugation.
Add 10 mL of DMEM/F12-10 medium and transfer the cell suspension into fresh 15 mL tubes.
Pellet the cells by centrifuging for 5 min at 200 x g at 20-25 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the cells into flow buffer-1 at a density of 1.0 x 10^7 cells per 100 µL of buffer.
Add FcR blocking reagent at a ratio of 1:100 and incubate for 5 min.
Add fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)-labeled CD31 antibody diluted 1:200 to the suspension.
Incubate the suspension for 30 min in the dark at 20-25 °C.
Add 10 mL of flow buffer-1 to the suspension.
Reserve 10 µL of the suspension for flow cytometry analysis.
Centrifuge the cells at 200 x g for 5 min at 20-25 °C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cells to a density of 1.0 x 10^7 cells per 100 µL of flow buffer-1 solution.
Add 5 µL of FITC selection cocktail per 100 µL of cell suspension.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting.
Incubate in the dark for 15 min at 20-25 °C.
Add 5 µL of magnetic nanoparticles per 100 µL of cell suspension.
Pipette well and incubate in the dark for 10 min at 20-25 °C.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 5 mL flow cytometry tube.
Add flow buffer-1 to achieve a total volume of 2.5 mL.
Place the flow cytometry tube in the magnet for 5 min.
Invert the magnet and decant the cell suspension containing cells that were not labeled with the FITC-CD31 antibody.
Maintain the magnet and tube in the inverted position for 2-3 s and then remove the remaining liquid.
Aspirate any droplets on the tube edge before returning the tube to an upright position.
Pick up the flow cytometry tube from the magnet and add 2.5 mL of flow buffer-1 to wash the remaining CD31+ cells.
Resuspend the cells by gently pipetting the cells up and down two or three times.
Place the flow tube into the magnet for 5 min.
Repeat steps for washing three times and then once more for a total of four washes.
Remove the flow tube from the magnet and add an indicated amount of suitable medium (e.g., human endothelial serum-free medium [hECSR] or freezing medium) to resuspend purified CD31+ cells.
Reserve two 10 µL aliquots of the suspension, one for cell counting and another for flow cytometry analysis to assess purity of CD31+ cells in post-MACS samples.
If a flow cytometer is not available immediately, store the aliquot at 4 °C until analysis.
Dilute vitronectin with dilution buffer to a final concentration of 10 µg/mL.
Transfer 500 μL of the diluted vitronectin solution to each well of the 12-well plates.
Leave the plates at 20-25 °C for at least 1 h.
Dissolve 5 mg of crystalized collagen type IV in 5 mL of sterile water.
Incubate the solution overnight at 4 °C.
Aliquot and store the incubated solution at -20 °C.
Dilute collagen IV aliquots 1:100 in sterile water to produce a 10 µg/mL solution.
Add 1 mL of the diluted collagen IV solution to each well of a 6-well plate.
Incubate the plates for at least 30 min at 37 °C.
Store the prepared plates at 37 °C for up to 1 week if needed.
Dissolve 500 µg of FGF2 in 5 mL of Dulbecco's PBS.
Add 7.5% BSA to a final concentration of 0.1%.
Aliquot the stock solution into volumes ranging from 20-200 µL.
Store aliquots at -20 °C for up to 3 months or at 4 °C for up to 1 month, avoiding freeze-thaw cycles.
Add 2 mL of B-27 supplement and 20 µL of FGF2 stock solution into 98 mL of hECSR medium.
Store the prepared hECSR medium at 2-8 °C for up to 2 weeks.
Add 15 mL of fetal bovine serum, 5 mL of DMSO, and 25 µL of ROCK inhibitor solution to 30 mL of hECSR medium to prepare freezing medium.
Store the freezing medium at 2-8 °C for up to 2 weeks.
Remove collagen solution from the 6-well plates.
Transfer 1.0-2.0 x 10^5 purified CD31+ EPCs in 2 mL of hECSR medium containing 5 µM ROCK inhibitor (1:2,000 dilution) to the 6-well plates.
Place the plate in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Evenly distribute the cells by gently sliding the plates back and forth, then side to side.
The next day, remove the hECSR medium containing ROCK inhibitor.
Add 2 mL of fresh hECSR medium without ROCK inhibitor.
Exchange the hECSR medium every other day until 100% confluence is reached.
Remove the hECSR medium from the 6-well plates containing a mixture of ECs and non-EC populations.
Add 1 mL of dissociation reagent to each well.
Monitor cell morphology under a microscope carefully, looking for bright and round ECs (typically within 2-5 min).
Detach the ECs by tapping the edge of the plate when they appear bright and round.
Collect detached ECs using a micropipette, taking care to avoid resuspending non-ECs.
Transfer collected ECs to a 15 mL or 50 mL centrifuge tube containing 4 mL of DMEM/F12 per 1 mL of dissociation reagent.
Add 2 mL of hECSR medium to the wells containing the remaining attached non-ECs to establish SMLCs.
Place the plate in the incubator.
Pipette the EC suspension in the centrifuge tube to mix thoroughly and reserve 10 µL of the suspension for cell counting.
Centrifuge the remaining cells for 5 min at 200 x g at 20-25 °C.
Remove the supernatant from the pellet and add 2 mL of hECSR medium per 1.0-2.0 x 10^5 ECs.
Upon removal of the collagen IV solution from a new 6-well plate, add 2 mL of EC suspension to each well.
Incubate at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
To evenly distribute the cells in the plate, gently move it in a back and forth and side to side motion on the incubator shelf.
Replace the hECSR medium every other day until the ECs reach 100% confluency.
Replace the hECSR medium every other day for SMLCs.
Pass collected SMLC-conditioned medium through a 0.22 μm filter upon each medium change.
Pool the SMLC-CM until the SMLCs reach 100% confluency.
Resuspend EPCs in freezing medium at a density of 1.0-2.0 x 10^6 cells/mL after the final MACS wash.
Distribute 1 mL of the cell suspension into cryotubes for freezing.
Place cryotubes with EPCs into a controlled rate freezing device and transfer to -80°C.
Move EPC tubes to liquid nitrogen tank 24 to 48 h after freezing for long-term storage.
Add dissociation reagent (1 ml/well) to EECM-BMEC-like cells or SMLCs and incubate at 37°C with 5% CO2 until cells detach (5-7 min and 20-30 min respectively).
Collect detached cells in a tube containing DMEM/F12-10 medium.
Pipette thoroughly to mix and reserve 10 μL of cell suspension for counting.
Centrifuge the cells at 200 x g for 5 min at 20-25°C.
Remove supernatant and resuspend cells in freezing medium to a density of 1.0-2.0 x 10^6 cells/mL.
Distribute 1 mL of cell suspension into cryotubes for storage.
Place cryotubes in a controlled rate freezing device.
Transfer cryotubes immediately to -80°C for initial storage.
Transfer tubes to liquid nitrogen tank 24 to 48 hours after freezing for long-term storage.
Roll vials of cryotubes between hands or incubate in a 37°C water bath until cells are nearly completely thawed.
Add 500 μL of DMEM/F12-10 and gently transfer cell suspension to a 15 mL tube containing 4 mL of DMEM/F12-10 medium.
Wash cryotube once by adding 1 mL of DMEM/F12-10, then centrifuge cells at 200 x g for 5 minutes at 20-25°C.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend pellet in 2 mL of hECSR medium containing 5 μM ROCK inhibitor (1:2,000 dilution) to a density of 1.0-2.0 x 10^5 cells per 2 mL for EPCs.
For EECM-BMEC-like cells and SMLCs, resuspend pellet in 2 mL of hECSR medium at a density of 2.0-3.0 x 10^5 cells per 2 mL.
Distribute cell suspension among wells of collagen-coated 6-well plates after aspirating the collagen solution.
Gently move plates back and forth, then side to side, on the shelf of an incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 to evenly distribute cells in the wells.
Exchange the medium with fresh hECSR medium lacking ROCK inhibitor.
Repeat medium exchange every other day until 100% confluency is achieved.
Proceed to selective passaging for EPCs after achieving 100% confluency.
Perform functional analyses for EECM-BMEC-like cells after reaching 100% confluency.
Seed the EECM-BMEC-like cells on filter inserts to develop complete monolayers.
Measure the permeability of sodium fluorescein in EECM-BMEC-like cell monolayers.
Conduct immunofluorescence staining to monitor expression of junctional molecules, adhesion molecules, or cytoskeletal proteins in EECM-BMEC-like cells.
Assess expression of cell surface adhesion molecules with or without inflammatory cytokine stimulation.
Analyze the expression of cell surface adhesion molecules on EECM-BMEC-like cells using flow cytometry.

Use flow cytometry to assess the semi-quantitative expression of ICAM-1, ICAM-2, VCAM-1, P-selectin, E-selectin, CD99, and PECAM-1 on cell surface adhesion molecules involved in immune cell migration into the CNS.
Culture EECM-BMEC-like cells with SMLC-conditioned medium in the presence and absence of inflammatory cytokines for 16 to 18 hours.
Perform an immune cell adhesion assay under static conditions to assess the expression of functional adhesion molecules.
Seed EECM-BMEC-like cells onto a chamber slide at a density of 5.5 x 10^4/cm² and allow them to grow to confluence.
Change the culture medium to SMLC-conditioned medium in the presence or absence of pro-inflammatory cytokines after approximately 24 hours.
Incubate the EECM-BMEC-like cells for an additional 16 hours.
Thaw cryopreserved immune cells with T-cell wash buffer.
Label thawed immune cells with fluorescent dyes in T-cell medium.
Add 2 x 10^4 Th1 cells to the EECM-BMEC-like cells in a 16-well chamber slide.
Incubate the immune cells and monolayer of EECM-BMEC-like cells for 30 min in migration assay medium.
Wash the slide gently twice with Dulbecco's PBS.
Fix the slide with 2.5% glutaraldehyde solution at 4°C for 2 h.
Wash the slide twice again with Dulbecco's PBS.
Mount the slide with a coverslip.
Acquire fluorescence microscopy images of the center of the monolayer on the slides to count immune cells attached to EECM-BMEC-like cell monolayers.
